rubrics.rubric: Does the composite scoring model include all five required factors: utilization rate, cost efficiency, service reliability (late shipment rate), customer satisfaction, and port connectivity?
criterion: The Composite_Score tab must incorporate a utilization rate dimension derived by comparing actual order volume from OrderList.csv against daily capacity from WhCapacities.csv for each plant.
The Composite_Score tab must incorporate a cost efficiency dimension using WhCosts.csv cost-per-unit data and/or FreightRates.csv.
The Composite_Score tab must incorporate a service reliability dimension measured via late shipment rate (Ship_Late_Day_Count > 0 in OrderList.csv).
The Composite_Score tab must incorporate a customer satisfaction dimension sourced from the Survey_Results sheet in Customer_Satisfaction_Survey_Q4.xlsx.

The Composite_Score tab must incorporate a port connectivity dimension from PlantPorts.csv, where plants with single-port access (16 of 19 plants) are flagged as higher risk, and all five factors must be operationalized with actual data, not merely listed.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Data_Reconciliation tab independently calculate the company-wide late shipment rate and compare it to the COO memo's stated '~2%' figure?
criterion: The Data_Reconciliation tab must compute the late shipment rate directly from OrderList.csv: 192 orders with Ship_Late_Day_Count > 0 out of 9,215 total orders = approximately 2.08%, and compare it against the COO memo's stated '~2%' figure.

The Data_Reconciliation tab should note that the computed figure (2.08%) is consistent with the memo's approximation and document any interpretation assumptions (e.g., whether Ship_Late_Day_Count > 0 is the correct definition of 'late,' whether the memo covers a different time period).

The reconciliation must also check whether all Plant_Codes in OrderList.csv appear in WhCapacities.csv and PlantPorts.csv, confirming no orphaned records exist (all 7 active plants are present in both reference files).

rubrics.rubric: Does the consolidation scenario verify that receiving plants will not exceed their warehouse capacity after absorbing redistributed volume?
criterion: For each proposed closure, the Consolidation_Scenarios tab must check WhCapacities.csv to confirm that the receiving plant(s) can handle the additional order volume without exceeding daily capacity.

The Consolidation_Scenarios tab must present specific capacity utilization calculations for receiving plants both before and after absorption, using actual unit quantities from OrderList.csv against daily capacities from WhCapacities.csv.

For example, PLANT03 has a daily capacity of 1,013 units and already handles 8,541 orders (92.7% of total volume); absorbing volume from smaller PORT04 plants (PLANT08 at 102 orders, PLANT09 at 12 orders) requires verifying PLANT03's post-absorption utilization remains feasible.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Risk_Matrix tab correctly cross-reference the Complaint_Log data with closure candidates and apply the customer attrition risk flag (severity >= High AND resolution rate < 70%)?
criterion: The Risk_Matrix must extract complaint data per plant from the Complaint_Log sheet with the correct distribution: PLANT03 (5 complaints), PLANT08 (3 complaints), PLANT09 (3 complaints), PLANT12 (2 complaints), PLANT13 (2 complaints), PLANT16 (2 complaints), PLANT04 (1 complaint).

For each closure candidate, the Risk_Matrix must calculate: number of open complaints (status other than 'Resolved'), average severity, unresolved complaint rate, and most frequent complaint category.

The attrition risk flag must be applied where any complaint has severity 'High' AND the plant's resolution rate is below 70% (e.g., PLANT09 has 3 complaints with 1 High-severity complaint C-014 and only 1 resolved out of 3 at 33% resolution rate, triggering the attrition risk flag).

rubrics.rubric: Does the analysis correctly calculate net cost impact for each consolidation scenario, incorporating both savings from closure and increased costs at receiving plants?
criterion: For each proposed plant closure, the response must calculate cost savings from closing the plant using WhCosts.csv cost-per-unit data and the plant's current order volume.
The response must calculate increased costs at receiving plants from handling additional volume, using both WhCosts.csv warehouse costs and FreightRates.csv for any changed freight routes.

The response must present a net annual cost impact (savings minus increased costs) for each scenario, using actual data values from WhCosts.csv (e.g., PLANT08's cost per unit is $0.5229 and PLANT03's is $0.5175).
Freight cost changes must also be considered if orders are rerouted through different carriers or modes.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Board Decision Brief include a Methodology Statement that explains the composite scoring approach, factor weights, and acknowledges data limitations?
criterion: The Word document must contain a Methodology Statement section (approximately 0.5 pages) that explains what factors were included in the composite score and why, and how weights were derived from data patterns.
The Methodology Statement must explain how the scoring model was constructed, including the normalization approach and aggregation method.

The Methodology Statement must explicitly acknowledge data limitations — critically, that only 7 of 19 plants have order data in OrderList.csv, that the customer satisfaction survey covers only a subset of plants, and that FreightRates.csv may not perfectly map to actual order routes; a methodology statement that claims completeness without noting these gaps fails this criterion.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Consolidation Recommendation section provide ranked closure candidates with all six required metrics per plant (utilization, cost per unit, late shipment rate, satisfaction score, redistribution plan, and net annual cost impact)?
criterion: For each of the 3-5 closure candidates, the Board Decision Brief must include: current utilization rate (actual orders vs. daily capacity from WhCapacities.csv), cost per unit from WhCosts.csv, and late shipment rate from OrderList.csv.

Each closure candidate must include a customer satisfaction score from the Survey_Results sheet and a proposed volume redistribution plan identifying which plant(s) will absorb the volume with port-sharing justification.
Each closure candidate must include a net annual cost impact estimate.

Each candidate must also include a brief counterargument for retention; strong closure candidates based on the data include PLANT08 (daily capacity 14, 17.65% late rate, shared PORT04), PLANT09 (daily capacity 11, only 12 orders, shared PORT04), and potentially zero-volume plants on shared ports.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Go/No-Go Matrix present a single-page summary table with a recommended action (Close, Consolidate, or Retain-and-Monitor) and one-line justification for each candidate plant?
criterion: The Board Decision Brief must include a Go/No-Go Matrix as a clear table with one row per closure candidate plant, covering all 3-5 identified candidates.
Each row must contain: the plant identifier, the recommended action (exactly one of: Close, Consolidate, or Retain-and-Monitor), and a concise one-line justification.

The recommended actions should logically follow from the preceding analysis — for example, a plant with shared port access, low volume, and no customer attrition risk might warrant 'Close,' while a plant with unresolved high-severity complaints might warrant 'Retain-and-Monitor' until complaints are resolved.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response correctly identify that PLANT03 handles approximately 92.7% of all order volume and assess the strategic implications of this extreme concentration?
criterion: The analysis must identify that PLANT03 processes 8,541 out of 9,215 orders (92.69%), making NovaTrans heavily dependent on a single facility with only single-port access (PORT04).

The analysis must discuss concentration risk implications: PLANT03 is critical infrastructure that cannot be consolidated, and any consolidation of other PORT04 plants into PLANT03 increases this concentration risk further.

The analysis must note that PLANT03's own late shipment rate (2.04%, representing 174 late orders) contributes the vast majority of late deliveries by volume, and should consider whether diversifying away from PLANT03 dependency might be more strategically important than closing small plants.
